title: Fynaptix · Nuclear & SMR Research
heading: Nuclear Energy Intelligence
subheading: Small modular reactors, uranium & the AI power-demand trade
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. SMR developers are pre-revenue with long regulatory timelines; verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Bloomberg reported Sep 18 that Westinghouse (49%-owned by Cameco) is now targeting a $50B+ US IPO valuation, up sharply from the ~$30B floated just weeks earlier; Cameco's stake alone would be worth roughly $24.5B — nearly two-thirds of Cameco's own $38.4B market cap — making this one of the most concrete, dated re-rating catalysts anywhere on this page

The House passed the bill Sep 16 requiring data centers over 100MW to fund their own new power and transmission infrastructure rather than socializing costs to ratepayers; Oklo and NuScale jumped 13% and 10% intraday on the news, then gave back most of it within two trading days once traders registered that a 417-3 House vote is a headline, not a Senate-passed law or a signed contract

Spot traded in a tight $89.85-$90.05/lb band the week of Sep 22 — up from $86.36 at the end of July but well off the year's highs — with analysts flagging $99/lb on the futures curve as the level that would confirm a genuine breakout rather than continued range-bound consolidation

Still zero, but TVA said Sep 9 it expects an NRC construction-permit decision on the Clinch River BWRX-300 "within weeks" — the most concrete near-term step toward an actual SMR groundbreaking — even as NuScale drew a fresh securities-fraud investor alert (Pomerantz, Sep 22) over ENTRA1 disclosures, a reminder that permitting progress and investor confidence aren't moving together

tiers.label: Operating / Cash-Generating Exposure
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Largest US nuclear fleet operator (55 GW post-Calpine); direct data-center PPAs with Microsoft, Meta, Walmart
rows.watch for: Shares recovered from last week's six-day, 13% slide to close at $263.27 (Sep 25), up ~3% on the week, while management kept actively reshaping the portfolio — a $715M deal to buy the Rhode Island State Energy Center from Shell, and an $860M sale of a Texas gas plant to LS Power — rather than just riding the AI-power narrative; Morgan Stanley's price target now sits at $369 and the average analyst target is $347.28 (+32% implied upside) against FY26 guidance of $11.50-$12.50/share

rows.angle: Major Western uranium producer + Westinghouse stake
rows.watch for: Shares slid further to $88.07 even as Bloomberg reported Sep 18 that Westinghouse (49%-owned by Cameco) is now targeting a $50B+ IPO valuation, up from ~$30B floated weeks earlier — Cameco's stake alone would be worth roughly $24.5B; 2025 revenue of $3.48B (+11% YoY) and net income of $589.6M (+243%) underpin the still-Buy-rated 21-analyst consensus with a $127.77 target (+45% upside)

rows.angle: Nuclear components, naval reactors, advanced reactor work
rows.watch for: Shares hit a third straight week of new 52-week lows ($138.47, down from $147.52), even after Fitch awarded BWXT its first-ever investment-grade rating (BBB, Stable) and it won a US Army Janus program contract plus a DOE lithium-processing-facility design award; management gets two chances to make its case in three days — a broader Investor Day Sep 29 and a William Blair investor meeting in New York Sep 30 — with consensus still Buy at an average $222.07 target (+60% upside) and ARK Invest adding $7.64M of shares this week

rows.angle: Grid equipment + BWRX-300 SMR design via GE Hitachi Nuclear Energy
rows.watch for: Shares held a $940-$960 range (closing $957.63 Sep 25, still up 49% over the past year) on a steady drip of international nuclear news rather than one big catalyst: GE Vernova Hitachi and Samsung C&T were selected for a 1.2 GW Swedish nuclear project, South Korea is being floated as a partner on US nuclear construction, and SHINE joined a GEV-led ARPA-E fuel-recycling initiative; nuclear remains a small slice of a $255B market cap that's still primarily a grid/gas-equipment story

tiers.label: Pre-Revenue SMR Developers — Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Fast reactors using recycled waste; Sam Altman-backed; deals directly with AI/data-center customers
rows.watch for: Shares slipped to $38.04, a 63.5% market-cap decline from 52-week highs near $193.84, after UBS cut its own price target to $41 from $55 this week even as Piper Sandler's Overweight/$55 call from Sep 10 remains in play; shares gave back most of their House-bill pop within two days (-5% to $37.57 on Sep 18), and the ~$1B ATM equity program from early September remains a live dilution overhang against Q2's first-ever revenue ($1.2M, beat by >1,000%) and a widened ~$48.5M net loss, though cash still stands near $1.64B

rows.angle: Only SMR design with NRC formal approval; utility-focused; 6 GW TVA/ENTRA1 collaboration announced
rows.watch for: Shares fell further to $8.42 (52-week range $7.21-$57.42, market cap down 31.9% from highs), confirming UBS's Sep 10 Sell/$6 call after a prior 12.5% single-day drop; a fresh securities-fraud investor alert from Pomerantz Law Firm on Sep 22 over ENTRA1-related disclosures adds legal risk on top of the still-unresolved question of whether the 6 GW TVA/ENTRA1 program becomes a firm, priced agreement, while a rival design (GE Vernova's BWRX-300 at Clinch River) looks closer to an actual NRC construction permit

rows.angle: HALEU enrichment — fuel for advanced reactors
rows.watch for: Centrus added a second dated HALEU supply contract this month — Radiant, alongside the existing Antares deal, both including customer prepayments and deliveries starting before year-end — and raised FY26 revenue guidance to $450-500M; shares closed at $147.07, still down ~40% from their 52-week high of $464.25, with a 19-analyst Buy consensus averaging a $247.40 target (+68% upside) against Jefferies' more cautious Hold/$169 call

private_watchlist.name: TerraPower
private_watchlist.note: Bechtel and TerraPower split on the next construction phase of the Kemmerer Unit 1 Natrium demonstration plant (reported Sep 18-19); Bechtel filed a WARN notice for ~200 Reston, VA positions, though it says most staff will be redeployed to other nuclear projects rather than laid off, and TerraPower says the site transition is designed to protect the existing construction schedule with no anticipated changes. TerraPower's CEO told Reuters (Sep 10) that Natrium reactors could begin generating power in the UK, its first market outside the US, by 2034.

private_watchlist.name: X-energy
private_watchlist.note: Shares fell 4.1% to $15.08 (52-week range $13.29-$37.10, market cap $6.13B) even as TRISO-X completed vertical construction at its TX-1 HALEU fuel fabrication facility in Oak Ridge this week — real physical progress on the fuel side of the business. Analyst views remain wide apart: a 9-analyst Buy consensus averages a $34.38 target (+128% upside), directly at odds with Piper Sandler's earlier Sell/$9 call. TRISO-X president Joel Duling is retiring effective Nov 20 after 40+ years with the company; DOE is separately backing X-energy's Texas Xe-100 project with up to $1B.

private_watchlist.name: Kairos Power
private_watchlist.note: No new update this week. Google's first-ever corporate agreement to develop a US SMR fleet remains up to 500 MW across 6-7 units, targeting a first commercial Hermes unit by 2030 and full fleet by 2035; the Hermes 2 demonstration plant at Oak Ridge, which broke ground in April 2026, continues construction.

private_watchlist.name: Commonwealth Fusion
private_watchlist.note: The cryogenic system for the SPARC tokamak in Devens, MA reached its full 8-kelvin operating temperature this month, chilling the toroidal-field magnets colder than the surface of Pluto — a key hardware milestone ahead of the targeted 2027 scientific-breakeven (Q>1) run. Total capital raised still stands at $4B following the $1B round that closed Jul 30.

private_watchlist.name: Helion
private_watchlist.note: Helion's Polaris prototype demonstrated measurable deuterium-tritium fusion and hit a plasma temperature of 150 million°C this month, a meaningful technical milestone. OpenAI remains reportedly in talks to buy power from Helion (potentially up to 5GW by 2030) alongside the existing Microsoft PPA (50MW by 2029 via the Orion plant, under construction); no new dated news on either commercial deal this week.

private_watchlist.name: Holtec Nuclear
private_watchlist.note: Holtec suspended its planned ~$900M Nasdaq listing (ticker HNUC) on Sep 16, per Bloomberg, after targeting a $10.2B valuation just over a week earlier; the CEO cited "a perfect storm" as sentiment turned against AI-data-center-linked investments. The S-1 remains on file but no new pricing date has been set. Underlying business is unchanged: $564M trailing revenue anchored by the Palisades restart and the SMR-300 microreactor program.

bear_case.title: A $50B Westinghouse valuation doesn't change that zero SMRs are operating
bear_case.description: Even the sector's biggest, most concrete near-term catalyst — a possible $50B+ Westinghouse IPO — sits on top of an industry where the operating-commercial-SMR count is still zero. Permitting timelines, construction execution, and financing risk for the pre-revenue developers haven't moved just because a 68-year-old reactor-services business is getting a rich valuation.

bear_case.title: The House-bill rally evaporated within two trading days
bear_case.description: Oklo and NuScale jumped 13% and 10% intraday on the Ratepayer Protection Act's passage, then gave back most of it by the next session (-5% and -7%) once traders registered that a 417-3 House vote needs the Senate and a presidential signature before it changes anyone's cash flows. Policy-driven pops in this sector keep proving to be trading events, not investment theses.

bear_case.title: NuScale now carries a securities-fraud investigation on top of a non-binding flagship deal
bear_case.description: Pomerantz's Sep 22 investor alert over ENTRA1-related disclosures adds a legal and governance overhang to a stock whose entire long-term case still rests on the 6 GW TVA/ENTRA1 program becoming a firm, priced agreement rather than a framework collaboration. Shares confirming UBS's Sell call at $8.42 suggest the market isn't waiting for that resolution.

bear_case.title: Analyst targets on the same stock now span $9 to $34
bear_case.description: X-energy's Piper Sandler Sell/$9 call versus a 9-analyst Buy consensus averaging $34.38 is one of the widest analyst dispersions in the sector — a sign that even professional coverage can't agree whether these valuations are supported by anything firmer than a total-addressable-market story, regardless of real construction progress like TRISO-X's completed TX-1 shell.

catalysts.title: Pomerantz Law Firm opens a securities-fraud investor alert into NuScale
catalysts.description: The investigation centers on alleged misrepresentations tied to the ENTRA1 collaboration and adds to an existing securities-fraud class action over the same issues.

catalysts.title: Westinghouse reportedly targets a $50B+ IPO valuation
catalysts.description: Bloomberg reported the target is up sharply from the ~$30B floated weeks earlier; Cameco's 49% stake would be worth roughly $24.5B, nearly two-thirds of Cameco's own market cap.

catalysts.title: Oklo and NuScale give back most of their Ratepayer Protection Act rally
catalysts.description: Both stocks jumped double digits intraday on the House vote, then fell -5% and -7% respectively by Sep 18 as Holtec's pulled IPO weighed on broader sector sentiment.

catalysts.title: House passes the Ratepayer Protection Act, 417-3
catalysts.description: The bill requires data centers over 100MW to fund their own new power and transmission infrastructure rather than passing costs to other ratepayers; it still needs Senate passage and a presidential signature.

catalysts.title: TVA expects an NRC construction-permit decision on Clinch River "within weeks"
catalysts.description: The GE Vernova BWRX-300 project would be a landmark step toward an actual SMR groundbreaking under the NRC's streamlined licensing process.

catalysts.title: X-energy's TRISO-X completes vertical construction at its TX-1 fuel facility
catalysts.description: The Oak Ridge, TN HALEU fuel fabrication plant advances toward interior buildout, concrete progress on the fuel-supply side even as the stock fell on the week.

positions.name: Cameco
positions.note: Shares slid further to $88.07 even as Bloomberg reported Westinghouse (49%-owned by Cameco) is now targeting a $50B+ IPO valuation, up from ~$30B floated weeks ago — Cameco's stake alone would be worth ~$24.5B, nearly two-thirds of Cameco's own $38.4B market cap; sizing up further as the embedded-value catalyst gets more concrete while the operating uranium business (2025 revenue +11%, net income +243%) is unchanged.

positions.name: Constellation Energy
positions.note: Shares recovered from last week's six-day slide to close at $263.27, up ~3% on the week, while management kept reshaping the portfolio (a $715M Rhode Island plant purchase, an $860M Texas gas-plant sale) rather than just riding the AI-power story; sizing up modestly as the pullback looks fully digested and Morgan Stanley's $369 target still implies real upside.

positions.name: BWX Technologies
positions.note: Shares hit a third straight week of new 52-week lows ($138.47, from $147.52) even after Fitch awarded BWXT its first-ever investment-grade rating and it won new Army and DOE contract awards; moving off Core to Watch until the Sep 29-30 Investor Day and William Blair meeting explain why a fundamentally improving, newly-rated business keeps getting sold.

positions.name: GE Vernova
positions.note: A steady drip of small international nuclear wins (a 1.2GW Swedish BWRX-300 project, South Korea floated as a US construction partner) kept shares in a $940-$960 range, but nuclear still isn't a big enough piece of a $255B, largely grid/gas-equipment market cap to justify more than Watch. Also sits in the Energy Storage sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Oklo
positions.note: Shares held near $38 even as UBS cut its own target to $41 from $55 this week and the stock gave back most of its 13% Ratepayer Protection Act pop within two trading days; a modest increase reflects the ~$1.64B cash cushion and first-ever quarterly revenue beat, but the ~$1B ATM program keeps this sized as a call option, not a core holding.

positions.name: Centrus Energy
positions.note: Centrus added a second dated HALEU customer this month (Radiant, alongside Antares, both with prepayments and deliveries before year-end) and raised FY26 revenue guidance to $450-500M; sizing up from 5% to 12% on two concrete commercial contracts stacked on the existing $900M+ DOE Piketon award, while keeping it Speculative given shares are still down ~40% from their 52-week high and EPS fell YoY even as revenue grew.

positions.name: NuScale Power
positions.note: Shares fell again to $8.42, confirming UBS's Sep 10 Sell/$6 call, and a Sep 22 Pomerantz investor alert opened a securities-fraud angle over ENTRA1 disclosures on top of the still-non-binding 6GW TVA/ENTRA1 program; nothing here argues for anything but Avoid.

positions.name: X-energy
positions.note: TRISO-X completed vertical construction at its TX-1 fuel facility this week — real physical progress — but shares still fell 4% on the day and analyst targets range from Piper Sandler's $9 Sell to a $34.38 Buy consensus; that dispersion is exactly why this stays Watch rather than a funded position.
